proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true reporting/admission lag is effectively 0 or varies over time, a fixed 1-week delay can misalign peak timing and induce systematic lead/lag errors around the apex.
proposals.rationale: Anchor specification matching prior best: SEIRS supports waning immunity across the season, fractional dynamics help capture sharp/peaky waves, and a 1-week delayed infection proxy aligns with short infection-to-admission lag while avoiding the instability seen at longer delays.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May shift peaks earlier than observed if admissions lag infections by ~1 week, degrading fit around rapid upswings/downslope and producing overly sharp leading edges.
proposals.rationale: No explicit delay as a robustness check when the hospitalization-rate series behaves like a near-contemporaneous proxy for incidence (e.g., rapid progression in older adults or reporting aligned to symptom onset week). Keeps the same peak-shape flexibility via fractional SEIRS.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Delay sensitivity: may increase rolling variability and mis-time sharp peaks (especially in high-peakiness series), potentially requiring compensatory parameter shifts that reduce forecast stability.
proposals.rationale: Shorter-than-3-week but longer-lag alternative to accommodate slightly slower infection-to-admission timing or administrative aggregation effects; retained within the requested 0–2 search while keeping the same SEIRS+fractional peakiness handling.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Can underrepresent the empirically observed lagged relationship between infections and admissions, leading to biased peak timing and poorer alignment on the downslope.
proposals.rationale: Direct infection-proxy observation without delay as a parsimonious baseline within the preferred SEIRS family; useful when the hospitalization-rate series is effectively proportional to contemporaneous infectious burden rather than lagged incidence.
